candidates.exact_span: The facility discharges into Corral Canyon, thence into Tijeras Canyon in segment number 20.6.4.105 of the Rio Grande Basin. The designated uses for intermittent stream, designated as segment number 20.6.4.98, are wildlife habitat, livestock watering, marginal warmwater aquatic life, and primary contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which receiving-water segment and designated uses govern the permit determines which water quality standards and derived effluent limits are in scope, which monitoring may be tied to receiving-water conditions, and whether applicability can be resolved when segment/use assignment is ambiguous.

candidates.exact_span: EPA was unable to approve section 20.6.4.98 of the NMWQS because the State did not submit a Use Attainable Assessment (UAA) to support an aquatic life designation that does not meet the CWA §101(a)(2) objective as required by 40 CFR 131.10(j)(1).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Federal non-approval of the cited standards section leaves the operative designated-use basis for limit derivation uncertain and can force an unresolved rather than established applicability state for standards-dependent limits and missing-evidence cases.

candidates.exact_span: Prior to submittal of UAA, the designated uses of the downstream perennial stream are applicable to the receiving water. Therefore, chronic aquatic life criteria are appropriate for RP screening.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether downstream perennial-stream uses substitute for the intermittent-segment uses, and whether chronic aquatic life criteria govern only reasonable-potential screening or operative permit limits, changes which numeric limits apply, what monitoring/analysis form may be required, and how to classify periods where the governing use/criteria basis is not established.

candidates.exact_span: Where these technology-based permit limits do not protect water quality or the designated uses, additional water quality-based effluent limitations and/or conditions are included in the NPDES permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The trigger for imposing water quality-based limits beyond technology-based controls determines whether additional enforceable numeric limits must be compared to reported measurements.

candidates.computation_change_reason: This frames when state water quality standards must yield permit limits stricter than technology-based guidelines, affecting which enforceable numeric limits are in the applicable set for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The previous permit established limits for total aluminum and total copper. These limits will be maintained.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Directly identifies total aluminum and total copper as maintained enforceable numeric discharge limits whose values and continued applicability govern exceedance determinations for reported metal measurements.

candidates.exact_span: In accordance with 40 CFR 122.45(c), total recoverable metal concentration must be established as effluent limitations.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether limits and reported results must be expressed and compared on a total recoverable basis, rather than another metal fraction or reporting form, changes both the applicable numeric limit for compliance comparison and the monitoring parameter/form that is required.
